global_briefing: Keep three things in mind. The Trump, Xi and Putin summit and the US-China summit produced no mineral export terms, so the status of antimony, tungsten and rare-earth licences is still unknown. Houthi escalation against Saudi Arabia raises the risk of diesel, freight and sulphur costs, which reach Chilean and Indonesian leach and HPAL operations through price more than physical shortage. Reports that US officials approved nearly 900,000 AI chips for China, and a California probe of Nvidia, put the AI build-out that drives data-centre power and copper demand under policy risk. Chile's economic contraction softens industrial metals demand, and the Essequibo report, which is single-source, adds jurisdictional risk if it proves true.
